trailheadDirection: From Seattle on US 2, turn left at Coles Corner and follow that road about 10 miles, then turn right onto White River Road and drive roughly 1.5 miles to a pullout on the left (the winter parking).
approach: From the White River Road winter pullout, cross to the right side of the road and follow the short trail, watching for a blue marker beside it; the crag sits about 200 feet from the road.
note: MP area page for the crag itself gives drive, winter pullout and 200 ft walk; no second page found.
previousAttempt: No page found for this crag.

trailheadDirection: Take I-90 Exit 38 and follow the road all the way around, passing under the I-90 overpass, to the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead lot; a Discover Pass is needed to park.
approach: From the Dirty Harry's Peak trailhead lot, follow the trail (or the fire academy road) over the bridge and bear right, about 15 minutes to the big leaning cedar at the start of Wayne's World. Walk back up beneath Darkside; Erikland is just to the right of Darkside.
note: Erikland page gives the access (cedar at start of Wayne's World, then under Darkside); Wayne's World page gives 15 min from the Farside trailhead; Exit 38 page identifies the Far Side parking lot and Discover Pass. Farside trailhead = Dirty Harry's lot is an inference from the Exit 38 page.
previousAttempt: Only sibling crag (Wayne's World) page found, 15 minute walk from Farside lot; low confidence, not written.

trailheadDirection: From the Mazama store, drive about 3.1 miles up Lost River Road to the Goat Wall Creek drainage and pull off nearby.
approach: From the Goat Wall Creek drainage pullout, hike uphill in the drainage, which narrows and gets brushy. Allow roughly 30 to 40 minutes depending on snow; the ice climb is the right-most one in this area.
note: The Standard route page (GPS identical to the stored crag coordinate) gives the drive, parking at the drainage and the walk; other routes on the crag (Goat's Beard Ice, Claymore) have no approach text.
previousAttempt: MP Goat Wall page only says 3 miles north of Mazama Store on Lost River Road; no parking spot or walk to the base

trailheadDirection: From US 2 at Leavenworth, drive up Icicle Creek Road to the Bridge Creek Campground junction, which is where the plowed road ends in winter.
approach: From the Bridge Creek Campground junction, follow the dirt road over the bridge to a gate on the right, go past it for about 100 feet, then turn uphill to the left toward the falls. The upper half is a steep slope of 30 to 45 degrees that avalanches often.
note: MP Hubba Hubba area page gives parking and walk; Icicle ice area page agrees the climbs are off Icicle Creek Road via US-2 through Leavenworth. No mileage from a fetched page, so none stated.
previousAttempt: No fetched page describes the way to Hubba Hubba (summitpost 403, forum reports need javascript)

trailhead: Dutch Henry Falls trailhead pullout (Jameson Lake Road)
trailheadDirection: From Wenatchee, drive east on US 2 past Waterville and Douglas and the junction with SR 182, then about 8 miles farther turn left on paved Jameson Lake Road; the north trailhead is about 4 miles along on the left, marked by a small preserve sign.
approach: From the Dutch Henry Falls trailhead pullout (Jameson Lake Road), follow the roughly half-mile path through open shrub-steppe to the creek below the falls, where the ice forms. The land is a conservation preserve, so no motor vehicles.
note: Sundance Kid is Dutch Henry Falls (4 mi up Jameson Lake Rd); WTA and a second guide agree on the pullout and short walk to the base of the falls; Butch Cassidy and Wild Bunch pages have no location text.
previousAttempt: MP Moses Coulee page gives a dirt road off Highway 2 only; no parking or walk

trailhead: Excelsior Campground road pullout (Mount Baker Highway milepost 40)
trailheadDirection: Drive east on the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to milepost 40 and park off the pavement on the old road to the closed Excelsior Campground and pump house.
approach: From the Excelsior Campground road pullout (Mount Baker Highway milepost 40), walk back west along the highway to the trail directly opposite milepost 40 and follow it uphill to the crag, staying on the path to spare the moss.
note: MP area page and a guide-service write-up agree on milepost 40 parking and the trail across the highway.

trailheadDirection: Drive US 2 through Tumwater Canyon to any roadside pullout near milepost 94, where the flow can be seen from the road.
approach: From the US 2 pullouts near milepost 94, find a safe way across the river, which is the main obstacle and may not be frozen at its slow stretches. Follow the bank to the Fall Creek drainage and hike up it through avalanche terrain, about 2 hours to Drury Falls; The Pencil is in the same drainage several hundred yards to the west.
note: Drury Falls and The Pencil pages (GPS matches the crag) give pullout, river crossing and drainage; Comic Book Hero and The Drip are elsewhere in the canyon (across from Castle Rock, near the dam) and are not covered.
previousAttempt: MP Tumwater winter ice page only says see the individual climbs and the canyon page; no parking or walk

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth on US-2, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and follow it west to Eightmile Campground.
approach: From Eightmile Campground walk a few hundred feet west along Icicle Creek Road, away from town, then turn right and climb the slope to the buttress.
note: MP Eightmile Buttress Ice area page (Getting There) agreeing with MP Eight Mile Area and the route page location; no route-specific detail beyond that.
previousAttempt: No fetched page describes the way in.

trailheadDirection: From Seattle take I-90 east to Exit 54 for Hyak, turn right onto WA-906 and keep on it past an immediate left, then after about 0.4 miles turn right into the Hyak Sno-Park (winter parking needs a daily fee or seasonal Sno-Park permit).
approach: From Hyak Sno-Park follow the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail (Iron Horse Trail) south for 3 miles, using the side snowshoe track if on snowshoes. Just before an information board on the left, find a narrow gully on the right, go down beside the creek from the culvert past two short ice steps, and bushwhack through downed trees to the falls, about 50 m off the trail.
note: MP Keechelus Lake Ice area page (Getting There) plus WTA Hyak Sno-Park driving directions; MP Keechelus Lake area places routes about 3.5 miles east of Hyak on the same trail.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 Exit 38 drive up the forest road system on Forest Road 9020 to the junction with Forest Road 9021, as far as snow allows (the usual winter way, instead of the summer trailhead at Exit 42).
approach: From the Forest Road 9021 junction walk the road about a mile, turn hard left onto spur 110, and a quarter mile before its hairpin leave the road and go up through the woods onto the open slope below the north bowl. Traverse along the base of that slope to directly beneath the couloir.
note: Two agreeing winter trip reports (Exit 38 / forest road approach to the entrance of the couloir); MP route page gives only the Exit 42 winter pull-off and no walk to the couloir. Road snow level decides how far a car gets.
previousAttempt: Area and route pages; walk-in to the couloir base is not described in detail.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 take Exit 47 for Denny Creek, cross the freeway and follow Forest Road 58 to the Denny Creek parking lots just past the campground (Northwest Forest Pass or Sno-Park permit).
approach: From the Denny Creek parking lots take the Melakwa Lake trail past Denny Creek up to Upper Melakwa Lake. From the lake go up the valley with the flows on your left, climbing steep firm snow in winter, under 30 minutes to the base of the Line of Fire cliff band on the northwest side of the lake.
note: MP Melakwa Flows area page (Melakwa Lake trail, flows up valley on the left) + trip report placing Line of Fire NW of Upper Melakwa Lake, under 30 min from camp; WTA for the drive.
previousAttempt: Route page gives only 'center of the flows'.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 Exit 38 follow SE Homestead Valley Road to Forest Road 9020, just before the road passes under the freeway, and drive about 0.2 miles to a pullout on the right at an old abandoned road.
approach: From the Forest Road 9020 pullout follow the old road south, then west toward the scree field under the wall; it is overgrown now, so expect some bushwhacking. At the scree stay on the road line to a small cut log, then turn uphill on a faint trail to the crag base, roughly 0.2 miles and under 20 minutes.
note: MP Black Ice Crag Drytooling Park approach + trip report on CYA at Black Ice Crag (0.2 mile adventurous approach, old road overgrown); assumes Upper Black Ice is the ice wall over that crag.
previousAttempt: Only the neighbouring Black Ice Crag page found; low confidence.

trailheadDirection: From Enumclaw drive SR 410 east toward Crystal Mountain to the signed Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout on the right, about 9.5 miles south of Greenwater.
approach: From the Skookum Falls viewpoint pullout cross the White River, the hardest part of the day; how you cross changes year to year. Then scramble the steep, soft slope up to the base of the falls.
note: MP Skookum Falls route page (pullout, crossing the river) + Northwest Waterfall Survey (viewpoint on SR 410, 9.5 miles south of Greenwater) + MP area page (SR 410 from Enumclaw) + visitrainier (steep soft scramble to base).
crag: Waterfall ice and mixed routes in the SW Cascades
previousAttempt: Route page location text; area page agrees on SR 410 from Enumclaw.

trailheadDirection: From White Pass drive east on US-12 for about 2.2 miles to the Dog Lake parking area; the Clear Creek Falls overlook lot itself is often snowed in.
approach: From the Dog Lake parking area walk about 10 minutes, with some bushwhacking, to the overlook above the falls, and drop to the creek above the lip. The falls are usually top-roped or rappelled from there, so the base is reached from above; use snowshoes in deep snow.
note: MP Clear Creek Falls route page (park near Dog Lake, 10 min with bushwhacking) + climber.org 2004 report (Dog Lake outlet 2.2 miles east of White Pass, snow hike to the top of the falls).
previousAttempt: Area page says only 'approach via HWY 12'.
